title: ING Reportedly Selling $500M Portfolio of Data Center Debt

tickers.name: ING Groep N.V. American Depositary Shares

summary:
The identity of the mystery seller auctioning a massive portfolio of data center loans has been linked to the Dutch bank ING in new reports. Bids for the asset bundle, which totals roughly $500 million and includes approximately a dozen loans, are due Nov. 19 and must be at least $10 million in size.

The portfolio contains debt tied to operators Vantage Data Centers and CyrusOne, as well as $25 million in financing for the Stargate project in New Mexico, a joint facility involving OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank. The sale follows a force majeure notice sent by Oracle to the Stargate developer and broader market anxiety over AI infrastructure spending after the U.S. midterms, including a call from Texas's incoming governor to stop new data center construction.

selectedTweets.text:
🦔Someone wants out of roughly $500 million in data center loans at once. Bloomberg reports an unnamed seller put a dozen loans up for bid, including a $25 million piece of OpenAI’s Stargate site in New Mexico, plus debt tied to big operators Vantage and CyrusOne. It’s one of the first auctions made up only of data center debt. The sale comes two days after the midterms, and Texas’s incoming Democratic governor has already called for an immediate halt on new data center construction.

My Take
I wrote about that New Mexico site in September. Oracle, the tenant, sent the developer a force majeure notice there, which is the legal clause a company uses to say events outside its control may let it off the hook. I’d sell a loan on that project too. Bloomberg didn’t name the seller and I won’t guess, but picking this week looks deliberate to me.

The rest of the market isn’t helping. The Nasdaq 100 fell as much as 6.4% today, and junk bonds tied to data center builders like CoreWeave took some of the worst hits. Loans like these normally trade in private, so outsiders rarely see a price. On Nov. 19, when bids come due, we get one. A steep discount would force every lender with similar paper to mark theirs down too, and I’d bet more sellers line up after that.

Hedgie🤗
